subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw core expose persisted per-cron lifecycle hooks that can run shell or webhook actions, and what trust boundary/API should own that behavior?
rationale: The remaining work defines public cron schema and can execute unattended commands or network calls, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve Narrow Core Hook API
options.body: Define an additive core cron hook or gate contract with security-reviewed command/webhook permissions, runtime phases, failure semantics, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

options.title: Keep Hooks External
options.body: Declare command cron plus plugin hooks as the supported path and document the plugin or ClawHub pattern instead of adding CronJob hooks to core.

options.title: Defer Public API
options.body: Leave the issue open as an acknowledged product gap until maintainers are ready to own the cron hook API and trust model.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Core Hook API
recommendation.body: Define an additive core cron hook or gate contract with security-reviewed command/webhook permissions, runtime phases, failure semantics, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on the cron schema/runtime surfaces and authored the most specific prior routing review for this issue.
